sources.claims_supported: Since 17 January 2025, specified in-contract price rises on new consumer contracts must be stated upfront in pounds and pence; out-of-contract customers should shop around.
Promoted broadband prices remain below list prices; September 2025 average monthly price differentials were £4.17 for standard, £6.84 for superfast and £7.94 for ultrafast dual-play bundles.

BT has run Black Friday broadband promotions and states that campaigns can extend for up to two weeks around Black Friday and Cyber Monday; its indexed page still refers to 2025, so it does not support a current 2026 offer.
EE says full 2026 Black Friday broadband details will be published closer to the event and provides clearly labelled 2025 examples, supporting the page's pre-sale status warning.
Providers run broadband offers throughout the year; Black Friday can be cheaper, but deals require analysis and comparison rather than assuming every promotion is good.
Common promotion types include reward cards, bill credits, monthly price cuts and extras; effective monthly cost is a useful comparison field.

research_summary: The live UK SERP is led by comparison services and provider campaign pages. Comparison pages combine postcode tools with roughly 800 to 1,500 words covering offer types, timing, effective monthly cost, switching warnings and FAQs. Provider pages are shorter and promotional. As of 23 August 2026, some pages are prepared for the 2026 event but confirmed offers are generally not yet published. The useful editorial opportunity is an evergreen, evidence-led buying method that clearly distinguishes confirmed dates and consumer rules from provisional or historic promotions.
depth_rationale: A 1,400-word minimum matches the upper end of the substantive editorial content visible across the three ranking comparison pages without duplicating their live deal inventories. The topic needs enough room for timing, provider coverage, a worked total-cost method, annual price-rise treatment, existing-customer advice, switching checks and six standalone FAQs. More words would risk padding before 2026 offers are live; fewer would omit decision-critical checks that ranking pages consistently include.
